title: Client failover window and deferred prefix commit for partial-stream cleanup
creator: Ava Chen
description: Design and implement a client failover grace window and deferred prefix commit mechanism to reduce accidental tombstoning of partial generations after client disconnects or transient network partitions. This ticket covers API semantics, runtime heuristics for commit vs tombstone, KV-prefix commit workflow, and a compatibility shim for older SDKs that don't provide explicit resume tokens.
updates: 2026-02-11: Kickoff meeting. Aligned on goals: avoid premature GC of partial outputs, bound memory growth, and preserve SLOs when clients reconnect.
2026-02-18: Prototype of deferred-commit state machine implemented in the serving runtime. Uses per-generation lease + soft grace TTL + commit decision window.
2026-02-25: Integration spike showed cases where tool/function calls with side effects complicate deferred commit semantics; flagged for product and legal review.
2026-03-02: Added compatibility shim plan for SDKs pre 1.4 that don't attach resume_metadata. Shim will derive a weak resume token from client-session and sequence hints.

2026-03-08: Benchmarked memory and KV growth. Deferred commit reduces immediate tombstones but increases ephemeral KV entries by ~12% at 95th perc for multi-turn sessions. Decided to cap grace window for P1 customers to 90s, P2 to 30s.
2026-03-12: Implementation branch opened: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1129. Added integration tests for several reconnect scenarios and functioncall-resume ordering.
Next steps: finish canary rollout, dashboard metrics, and add customer-facing docs about resume semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Server preserves partial generations for the configured failover window instead of tombstoning immediately on client disconnect or timeout.
Resume handshake returns stable prefix state and allows client to request continuation without duplication or corruption of structured outputs.
Deferred commit path correctly converts ephemeral KV prefixes into committed state when conditions are met (client ack, full generation, or forced commit policy).
Compatibility shim allows older SDK clients to resume in at least 80% of typical reconnect cases without requiring SDK update.
No regression in tail latency >2% for P1 workloads during canary with default grace windows enabled.
Comprehensive unit, integration, and chaos tests added to CI with deterministic simulation of disconnects and delayed tool call responses.
tech_decisions: Use a three-state lifecycle for a generation: active -> deferred (soft-lease) -> committed/tombstone.
Deferred leases anchored to generation_id + kv-prefix key; lease renewal is idempotent and tied to client resume token when available.
Introduce a lightweight resume-token shim for older SDKs that encodes (session_id, approximate-offset, monotonic-drop-counter) with HMAC to prevent accidental clashing.

Tool/function-call side effects are only considered committed when the generation is committed; until then tool-call results are stored as quarantined artifacts and replayed or invalidated on commit/tombstone decision.
Cap the deferred grace window per customer tier to bound ephemeral KV growth. Provide auto-eviction heuristics if system pressure crosses thresholds.
implementation_notes: Runtime: add deferred_lease metadata to generation records, persisted to KV with lease_expiry and attempt_count.
API: extend streaming close frame with optional final_commit_hint that SDKs can set to request immediate commit on polite disconnect.
SDK: new SDK version 1.4 exposes explicit resume_metadata; older SDKs rely on compatibility shim. Document the new flag and safety guarantees.
Observability: emit metrics generation.deferred_count, generation.commit_latency, generation.forced_tombstones, and meter quarantined_tool_calls.
Testing: build simulated network layer that injects disconnects between token N and N+M and asserts no duplication of structured JSON outputs on resume.
test_plan: Unit: lease state transitions and HMAC-based shim token validation.
Integration: end-to-end resume from client SDK, server deferred-to-commit flow, and replay of quarantined tool call results.
Chaos: randomized disconnects with heavy functioncall load to validate quarantined artifact cleanup.
Performance: canary load with P1 traffic to measure tail latencies and KV read/write amplification.
Backward compatibility: run matrix of client SDK versions (1.2, 1.3, 1.4) against runtime and verify success rates.
rollout_plan: Beta: Enable feature for internal org + small set of customers with high tolerance for debug feedback.
Canary: 5% traffic on host clusters with metrics monitoring and automatic rollback if commit_latency or tombstones spike.
Gradual: increase to 25% then 100% with tiered grace window defaults applied by customer category.
Fallback: server-side toggle to disable deferred leases quickly and convert all deferred entries to tombstones in emergency.
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboards: deferred-lease count by customer, avg lease duration, forced-tombstone rate, quarantined-toolcall backlog.
Alerts: forced-tombstone-rate > 0.5% in 5m, deferred-kv-growth > 150% baseline for 10m, commit-failure-rate > 1%.
SLOs: maintain 99.95% streaming availability and <5% tail latency increase on canary.
